## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Guhaṭṭhakasuttaniddesa* (Mnd 2), translated as the *Exposition of the Eight on the Cave*, is the second text of the *Mahāniddesa* in the Khuddaka Nikāya. It serves as an early canonical exegetical treatise commenting upon the *Guhaṭṭhaka Sutta* of the Sutta Nipāta's *Aṭṭhakavagga*. In doctrinal discussion, the *Guhaṭṭhakasuttaniddesa* specifically elaborates on how the minds of noble disciples (*ariya*) at different spiritual attainments are freed from varying types and degrees of defilements [Jantrasrisalai 2008].

 Resembling parallels also appear in the *Mahābyūhasuttaniddesa* (Mnd 13), the *Dhammasaṅgaṇī*, and the *Saṃyutta Nikāya* (SN 4.10). Computational analysis by DharmaNexus reflects this dense intertextuality, detecting 6,809 matching segments shared with 264 Pali texts; the most extensive reuse occurs in other Niddesa texts such as the *Purābhedasuttaniddesa* (Mnd 10), *Khaggavisāṇasuttaniddesa* (Cnd 23), *Tuvaṭakasuttaniddesa* (Mnd 14), and *Jarāsuttaniddesa* (Mnd 6), as well as the *Mahāniddesa-aṭṭhakathā*, the *Nidāna Saṁyutta* (SN 12), and the *Catukkanipāta* (AN 4) [DharmaNexus]. Furthermore, DharmaNexus automatically aligns passages from this text with northern Buddhist literature, including the Sanskrit *Arthaviniścayasūtra*, Śāntideva's *Śikṣāsamuccaya*, the *Śrāvakabhūmi* of the *Yogācārabhūmi*, and Tibetan translations of the *Śatasāhasrikā Prajñāpāramitā* and the *Vinayavastu* [DharmaNexus].
